dispositions.method: Round two of 1773. The sweep check of 24 and 25 November 2026 (X-THIN-SWEEP; outputs/story_discovery_1779/sweep_check_25nov.md) read every passage of the 1773 pages shared word for word by 4 or more papers that no counted opening of round one explains, looked each up in the year's lists and counted it by its own opening words against every page of the year in both transcriptions. It found one item printed by every paper that survives for its weeks, which round one's lists did not name; asked, the owner chose on 25 November 2026 to admit it as the rule reads. Every printing was checked against its page scan by AI reviewers (scan_batches/round2.json, SCAN_PROTOCOL.md; verdicts in scan_verdicts/round2*.json).
dispositions.selection_rule: As in round one (Y-THIN as amended, B1): an item printed by every newspaper that survives for its weeks is admitted. The letter from the Lord Camden is printed by all 4 papers of its weeks.

counted_item_by_item.The letter from the Lord Camden: 4 of the 4 papers that survive for its weeks (MS 2 September, NHG 3 September, VG1 and VG2 9 September), counted by its own opening; the New-Hampshire Gazette introduces the same letter in its own words ('A letter from on board the Lord Cambden East Indiaman ... says'), counted with the others (C-02).
